userPosition: Legalizing drugs reduces harm and mass incarceration
counterPosition: Drug legalization increases usage, addiction rates, and societal costs despite reducing arrests
content: Cerdá and coauthors (JAMA Pediatrics, 2017) used Monitoring the Future survey data on 253,902 students in grades 8, 10 and 12 to compare Washington and Colorado before and after recreational marijuana legalization in 2012 with other states. In Washington, perceived harmfulness of marijuana declined 14.2% among eighth graders and 16.1% among tenth graders, while marijuana use increased 2.0% and 4.1%. In states that did not legalize, perceived harmfulness decreased 4.9% and 7.2%, and use decreased 1.3% and 0.9%. Legalization also creates commercial industries with a profit motive to increase consumption.

citations.author: Magdalena Cerdá, Melanie Wall, Tianshu Feng, Katherine M. Keyes, Aaron Sarvet, John Schulenberg, Patrick M. O'Malley, Rosalie Liccardo Pacula and others
citations.title: Association of State Recreational Marijuana Laws With Adolescent Marijuana Use
citations.studyType: Difference-in-differences analysis of repeated cross-sectional surveys

limitations: The cited study covers adolescent use in Washington and Colorado. It does not cover overdose deaths, Portugal, adult use or traffic fatalities; those figures were removed.
